gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180's ECO mode turns its AC outlets off when the load stays under a set 15–30 W for 1–4 hours, or that a Traeger D2 grill draws only about 10–20 W once it is up to temperature (0.08–0.17 A at 120 V, per Traeger), so with ECO on the outlet can switch off and the fire goes out mid-cook.
standout_why: I compared Traeger Support (the only page ChatGPT cited every time; it gives D2 running amps but says nothing about inverters or power stations), the Pit Boss 3 Series manual (cited; it covers only the 1,000 W inverter for ignition), Volt & Valley, the BLUETTI pellet-grill blog, the EcoFlow pellet-smoker guide and our own current page. None of them mentions ECO mode, AC auto-off, low-load shutoff or a station's outlet-timeout rules. EcoFlow and our page cover pure sine wave only. The BLUETTI blog says WiFIRE Traegers draw a steady 10–20 W but never links that to its own ECO cutoff. I score it 2 rather than 3 because I could not source the ECO default or threshold for the Elite 200 V2, Elite 100 V2 or Explorer 1000 v2, so it can't yet rank one station above another.
decides: This doesn't change capacity sizing (about 1 kWh still fits a 12-hour cook). It adds a required setup step and a comparison column. On any BLUETTI unit, ECO must be off before an overnight cook, because a D2 Traeger idling at about 10–20 W sits below the AC180's lowest selectable 15–30 W cutoff. Anker's C1000 outlets shut off only when no plug is detected for 15 minutes, with no wattage rule, so a plugged-in grill keeps power. That makes the Anker C1000 (the card ChatGPT showed at $449.99) the safer choice if the shopper won't change settings. Anker's −20 °C to 40 °C discharge range also covers a cold overnight cook.

findings.label: ECO mode AC auto-off threshold and delay
findings.value: AC output turns off when the load stays below a user-set 15–30 W (DC: 5–10 W) for 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 manual, page 18 (5. Appendix, FAQ Q4), ManualsLib mirror, English text
findings.note: Quoted: 'You can set the power threshold of AC output and DC output to 15-30W /5-10W, respectively, for 1, 2, 3, or 4 hours' and 'the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.' This is a mirror of BLUETTI's manual. I could not read the text of the BLUETTI-hosted PDF (cdn.shopify.com AC180_User_Manual.pdf); it would not parse. The page gives no default threshold or delay.

findings.label: Running current after heat-up, 120 V
findings.source_title: Grill Watt & Amp Usage – Traeger Support
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.08 A × 120 V = 9.6 W and 0.17 A × 120 V = 20.4 W. The whole range sits below or inside the AC180's 15–30 W ECO cutoff, so ECO can switch off the outlet during a long cook. Non-WiFIRE grills run 0.4–0.8 A (48–96 W) after heating, which is above the cutoff. Traeger lists Touchscreen grills at a single 95 W with no running figure. The page mentions generators but not inverters or power stations.

findings.label: AC outlet auto-off rule
findings.value: Outlet turns off only if no plug is detected for more than 15 minutes; with outputs off and no load, the unit powers off after 12 hours (standby time can be set in the Anker app)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000/C1000X Portable Power Station USER GUIDE (A1761), en-GB
findings.note: Quoted: 'The AC outlets can intelligently identify whether a plug is inserted' and they turn off 'if no plug is detected for more than 15 minutes.' The guide states no wattage threshold, so a plugged-in grill drawing 10–20 W should keep the outlet on. This is the en-GB edition of the A1761 guide, so check it against the US edition. It covers the C1000 Gen 1 (the card ChatGPT showed), not the Gen 2.

findings.label: Discharge temperature range
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000/C1000X Portable Power Station USER GUIDE (A1761), en-GB
findings.note: This matters for cold overnight cooks. The unit can run the grill below freezing but can't be recharged below 0°C.
